19. MongoDB discontinued on-premises Charts in September 2021. A MongoDB staff member wrote on 2022-02-01: "The on-prem version was discontinued last September. We did include a notice about this for around a year before support ended." https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/is-mongodb-charts-discontinued/144944 20. Search snippets give the exact on-prem end-of-life date as 2021-09-01. The primary notice host (mongosilverback.net) did not resolve, and the MongoDB lifecycle page has no Charts row, so this exact day is only partly confirmed. https://www.mongodb.com/legal/support-policy/lifec

24. Using unauthenticated embedding for sensitive data is an anti-pattern. MongoDB says unauthenticated access "is less secure and should only be used for charts that display non-sensitive data." This is from a search summary of the Manage Data Sources page. https://docs.mongodb.com/charts/saas/manage-data-sources 25. Allowing filtering on fields that reveal sensitive data is an anti-pattern. By default, embedded charts allow no filter fields until the author adds at least one. https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/filter-embedded-charts/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/embed-chart-anon-au

1. Charts builds one aggregation pipeline per chart. The segment order is: charts views, embedding pre-filters, dashboard filters, chart query, lookup fields, calculated fields, embedding filters (including injected filters), chart filters, encoded fields, sorting, then the maximum document limit. https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/aggregation-pipeline-generation.md 2. Charts skips any segment the author did not configure. https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/aggregation-pipeline-generation.md 3. Authors can inspect the generated pipeline with "View Aggregation Pipeline" in the Chart Builder.

**Scope.** In: the mechanisms that make a Charts usage pattern harmful, their limits, history, failure modes and disagreements. Out: siblings (SDK/REST surface, access control, cost model, chart-type catalogue, auth providers), general MongoDB schema anti-patterns and general query tuning. The parent's heatmap row and `tenantId: 'acme'` snippet are not counted as evidence. Claims that refine them are listed under Deltas.

Framing caveat: MongoDB does not publish a page called "Charts anti-patterns." The Charts docs navigation has no such section (https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/). The concept is a synthesis of warnings that are spread across individual docs pages. Each claim below cites the page where the warning appears.

In scope: the operational anti-patterns in Atlas Charts, meaning query shape, pipeline ordering, indexing, result-size limits, caching and refresh, workload placement, embedding authentication, and filter security. For each one the report covers the trade-off, how to check for it, and what it means in practice.

Out of scope: sibling concepts (the cost model, analytics-node configuration, the Embedding SDK API as a whole, chart types), general MongoDB schema anti-patterns (Atlas Performance Advisor), and general aggregation tuning.
**Out of scope:** general MongoDB schema anti-patterns, the SDK and REST API surface, the access-control model and the cost model as topics in their own right. Those are sibling frontier items.
